title: Rabbi Abba bar Yaakov
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: A student of Rabbi Yochanan, for we always find him speaking in the name of Rabbi Yochanan: Ketubot 77a, Gittin 59, Bava Metzia 38b (where the name is given as Rabbi Abba son of Rabbi Yaakov), Yerushalmi Sheviit ch. 1 halakha 1, Terumot end of ch. 5, Kilayim ch. 7 halakha 4, Maaserot ch. 1 halakha 2, Maaser Sheni ch. 1 halakha 1, Chagigah end of ch. 1, Yevamot ch. 2 halakha 12, Sotah ch. 8 halakha 2, Bava Metzia ch. 3 halakha 4.

So too we find him speaking in the name of Rabbi Yitzchak Rova (Berakhot ch. 6 halakha 1, 41a), but we do not find that he spoke with them directly. As for what we find in Sanhedrin 27a, that he was in Babylonia, where it says there that Bar Chama killed a person and the Exilarch said to Rav Abba bar Yaakov, 'Go out and examine it,' and he wished to find him liable while Rav Papi found a merit for him, Hyman considers it clear that it should read Rav Acha bar Yaakov, as in the reading of Dikdukei Soferim, since Rav Papi lived later, as a pupil of Rava.

notes.text: Hyman proposes Acha bar Yaakov in place of Abba in the Sanhedrin episode. This is a textual proposal, not a merger of the named sages.

The consulted Sanhedrin 27a–27b account actually reads Rav Abba bar Yaakov and includes Rav Papi’s intervention. Hyman’s proposed Acha reading and chronological argument remain his; the exact Dikdukei Soferim witness was not independently inspected. Reporting in another sage’s name is kept distinct from Hyman’s explicit statement that direct conversation is not found.
